harness.name: ai-harness-framework
harness.note: Written against the harness at this commit, including D-029: a required verification layer that only reports SKIP fails verify-feature. Replace this file to plan for another harness.

requirements.assumption: An agent can verify its own changes: every feature passes real verification layers, and a layer that only reports SKIP counts as nothing (D-029).
requirements.required: Before a feature edits a module, capture its current behavior with characterization tests (golden-master style) and make the test layer run them. Add an AGENTS.md rule: the agent that changes logic is never the only author of its tests.
requirements.recommended: Grow tests in the modules agents will touch first, and keep feature scopes inside green modules.
requirements.why: Without real tests, every required test layer reports SKIP and fails verify-feature, so no feature can pass honestly.

requirements.assumption: Wrong changes are caught before they run, by static types or a type checker in the typecheck layer.
requirements.required: Add a type checker for the main dynamic language in check mode, with a baseline so existing code passes and new code is checked; point the typecheck layer at it and record the baseline as a dated deferral.
requirements.recommended: Raise the checker's strictness for new and touched modules.
requirements.why: Dynamic code without a checker lets an agent's type mistakes through every static layer.

requirements.assumption: An agent finds every caller of the code it changes by reading and searching the code.
requirements.required: List the files with computed-target calls in AGENTS.md as "find every call target before editing", and add a lint rule to the lint layer that rejects new eval and computed-name calls (for example ESLint no-eval and no-implied-eval, RuboCop Security/Eval, Bandit B307).
requirements.recommended: List the files with computed-target calls in AGENTS.md as "find every call target before editing".
requirements.why: A call whose target is computed at run time does not show up when an agent searches for the method it renames or changes, so the agent breaks callers it never saw.

requirements.assumption: Files and the context needed to change them fit in an agent's working context.
requirements.required: Add an AGENTS.md rule to work one module at a time, and list the oversized files: plan edits by function there, and split a file before adding features to it.
requirements.recommended: List the largest files in AGENTS.md as split-before-feature files.
requirements.why: Large files push the relevant code out of an agent's context and invite confident edits to code it has not read.

requirements.assumption: A feature can be scoped to one module, so one agent, or one lane, owns the files it changes.
requirements.required: In AGENTS.md, treat each strongly coupled module pair as one area: a feature that touches either module plans for both, and parallel lanes never take the two modules of a coupled pair (the harness's arch-002 does not stop two lanes from editing the same files).
requirements.recommended: List the strongly coupled module pairs in AGENTS.md, so a feature touching one plans for the other.
requirements.why: When changes usually spill across modules, an agent scoped to one module leaves the other half of the change undone, and parallel agents on neighbouring modules collide.

requirements.assumption: Project-specific conventions are written down where agents read them.
requirements.required: Write the project's non-standard practices as rules in AGENTS.md, and fill docs/ARCHITECTURE.md by hand: the harness placeholder check passes generic template text (maideps/ai-harness-framework#23).
requirements.recommended: Add the non-standard practices that are still unwritten to AGENTS.md, and record significant decisions in DECISIONS.md.
requirements.why: Agents follow written rules; unwritten local conventions are exactly what they get wrong (arXiv 2602.11988).

requirements.assumption: The project builds and verifies with scripted, repeatable steps.
requirements.required: Add what the evidence shows missing: CI from the harness template (templates/ci.yml), a pinned runtime version, a test runner, and a lock file where the ecosystem uses one.
requirements.recommended: Add the remaining missing signal so every verification run is reproducible.
requirements.why: init.sh and the verification layers can only be trusted when the environment they run in is pinned and scripted.

requirements.assumption: Verification runs on a supported runtime that matches production.
requirements.required: Run the verification layers under the declared legacy runtime (a container or a pinned toolchain in CI), separately from the harness's own Node 18 or later, and keep agents away from runtime-sensitive code paths without that toolchain.
requirements.recommended: Plan the runtime upgrade before the runtime reaches end of life, and run CI on both the current and the next runtime.
requirements.why: Code verified on a different runtime than it ships on is not verified.

stackDetection.change: Declare each verification layer command explicitly in package.json scripts (for example phpunit, bin/rails test, make check), so no required layer reports only SKIP.
stackDetection.why: The harness picks layer commands from root markers; when it does not detect the repository's main language, its layers run the wrong tool or SKIP, and a SKIP-only required layer fails verify-feature (D-029).

red.change: List these paths as proposal-only in AGENTS.md, and add Claude Code permissions.deny rules so agents cannot edit them directly; agents propose diffs for a person to apply.
red.why: Auth, billing, permission and secret code needs human review of every change.

yellow.change: List these modules in AGENTS.md as characterization-tests-first: no feature work there until their current behavior is pinned by tests.
yellow.why: Agents may only edit autonomously where their changes can be verified.
